title: Grade 8 Common Core Math — Answer Key
id_format: S<set>-<section>-Q<number>; section is M (main), B1, B2, ... (backward), F1 or F2 (forward)
grading_rules: Match each student response to its key record by the question ID printed on the question page (for example S40-F2-Q3). The page number is the same in the Question Collection and the Answer Key. IDs are unique within one grade's collection; across collections use uid (for example G5:S40-F2-Q3).
Multiple choice and true/false: the response is correct when the chosen letter equals correct_letter, or when the student wrote the text of the correct choice.

Short answer: accept any mathematically equivalent form unless the question asks for a specific form (equivalent fractions, decimals, and mixed numbers; a ratio written as a : b, a to b, or a/b; "x = 5" or "5"; terms of an expression in any order). Units are not required unless the question asks for them.
When an answer has several parts (separated by semicolons, or with labels such as "Rate of change:"), every part must be correct.
Drawing / plotting questions (type plot): correct_answer describes what a correct drawing shows. Judge the student's drawing against it.

Drawing + written questions (type plot_text): the student draws on the figure AND writes an answer. drawing_answer describes the correct drawing and correct_answer the written answer. Both must be correct: every requested point, segment or shape in the drawing, and the written conclusion.

Answer with required work (type work): required_method says what the shown work must use. A correct final answer without that work earns partial credit only; correct work with a slip in the final answer is also partial.
Explain / describe questions: grading_note says what a correct response must include; accept any reasonable wording.
grading_note also lists other accepted answers and the work behind an answer. It is guidance for the grader, not for students.

questions.section_title: Prove that the elimination step keeps the same solutions
questions.question: System A: x + y = 9 and x - y = 3. System B: x + y = 9 and 2x = 12 (its second equation is the sum of the two equations of A). Show that every solution of A is a solution of B, and every solution of B is a solution of A.
questions.correct_answer: The systems have the same solutions; both have only (6, 3).
questions.required_method: Both directions are required. A to B: if (x, y) makes both equations of A true, adding them gives 2x = 12, so (x, y) solves B. B to A: if (x, y) solves B, subtracting x + y = 9 from 2x = 12 gives x - y = 3, so (x, y) solves A.

questions.question: Triangles ABC and DEF have AB = DE, angle A = angle D, and AC = DF (SAS). Explain the rigid motions that map triangle ABC onto triangle DEF, and why C must land on F.
questions.correct_answer: A rigid motion maps A to D, B to E, and C to F, so the triangles are congruent.
questions.required_method: A complete argument: translate A to D; rotate so ray AB lies along ray DE, and B lands on E because AB = DE; if C is on the other side of DE from F, reflect across DE. questions.correct_answer: C lands on F, so the triangles are congruent.
questions.required_method: Because angle A = angle D, the image of ray AC lies along ray DF; because angle B = angle E, the image of ray BC lies along ray EF. C is on both rays, and the two rays meet at only one point, F.

questions.required_method: A valid chain of reasons. Other valid orders are accepted. A conclusion without reasons is not full credit. Example: draw line l through C parallel to AB. questions.correct_answer: The three angles fill a straight angle, so they add to 180°.
questions.required_method: The three angles, one of each kind, together fill a straight angle, which measures 180°. So angle A + angle B + angle C = 180°. Any equivalent explanation is accepted.

questions.correct_answer: Angle A + angle B + angle C = 180°
questions.required_method: Angle 1 = angle A and angle 3 = angle C (alternate interior angles, because the line is parallel to AC). Angles 1, 2, and 3 together form a straight angle, so angle A + angle B + angle C = 180°.

questions.set_title: Give informal arguments for the triangle angle sum and the exterior angle of a triangle
questions.section_title: Grade 8 main question
questions.question: Use the triangle angle sum to explain why the exterior angle at C of triangle ABC equals angle A + angle B.
questions.correct_answer: The exterior angle at C = angle A + angle B
questions.required_method: The exterior angle and angle C form a linear pair, so exterior angle = 180° - angle C. The triangle's angles add to 180°, so angle A + angle B = 180° - angle C. Therefore exterior angle = angle A + angle B.

questions.question: In the figure, lines m and n are parallel. A translation along the transversal t carries line n onto line m. Use this translation to explain why angle 2 = angle 6.
questions.required_method: The translation moves the point where t meets n to the point where t meets m, keeps t on itself, and carries n onto m (they are parallel). So it carries angle 2 onto angle 6. A translation keeps angle measures, so angle 2 = angle 6.

questions.question: Lines m and n are cut by transversal t, and a pair of alternate interior angles is congruent. Explain why m and n must be parallel. (Suppose they meet at a point P, and look at the triangle formed with t.)
questions.required_method: A complete argument: if m and n met at P, they would form a triangle with t. One of the congruent angles would be an exterior angle of that triangle and the other a remote interior angle. But an exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, so it is greater than either one. That is a contradiction, so m and n do not meet: they are parallel.

questions.set_title: Use the angle-angle criterion to show that triangles are similar
questions.section_title: Establish the angle-angle criterion with similarity transformations
questions.question: Triangles ABC and DEF have angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E. Explain why a similarity transformation maps triangle ABC onto triangle DEF.
questions.correct_answer: Dilate ABC by the scale factor DE ÷ AB, so the image of AB has the same length as DE. Rigid motions then move that image onto DE (A onto D, B onto E), with the third vertex on the same side as F. Because angle A = angle D and angle B = angle E, the image's other two sides lie along rays DF and EF, and two rays meet in only one point, so the third vertex lands on F. (The third angles are then equal too.)
questions.grading_note: Full credit needs the dilation, the rigid motions, and why the third vertex must land on F.

questions.set_title: Use relative frequencies in a two-way table to describe a possible association
questions.section_title: Recognize conditional probability and independence in everyday situations
questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
questions.question: Explain the difference between P(sleeps under 8 hours | uses a phone at night) and P(uses a phone at night | sleeps under 8 hours).
questions.correct_answer: The first is the chance that a night phone user sleeps under 8 hours; the second is the chance that a person who sleeps under 8 hours uses a phone at night. The condition (the group you look in) is different.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Conditional Probability & the Rules of Probability
questions.question: A fair coin is flipped twice, and the flips are independent. Is P(second flip is heads | first flip is heads) equal to P(second flip is heads)? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. Both are {1/2}; the first flip does not change the second.
